decoy_bugs.summary: With the known-key feature, KnownKey::lookup and lookup_mut return None for keys that are present once a BorrowedValue object has more than 32 entries and halfbrown has moved it from vec storage to hash storage.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: KnownKey::lookup, map_lookup, lookup_mut or map_lookup_mut (src/known_key.rs:95-201) is called on an object with 33 or more entries built by to_borrowed_value. It returns None, or with lookup_mut fails to find the key, for a key that is present. The same key is found by the Index operator and by Value::get.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: map_lookup passes the hash cached in KnownKey::from (known_key.rs:63, NotSoRandomState::default().hash_one) to raw_entry().from_key_hashed_nocheck (known_key.rs:132/201). Once halfbrown switches to its hashbrown backend, that raw-entry probe uses the precomputed hash against buckets filled by the map's own hasher.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran tests/probe_kk.rs in a copy of the crate (tmp/c) with `cargo test --features known-key`. It builds objects of 1, 31, 32, 33, 64 and 1000 entries with to_borrowed_value, then looks up the first key, the last key and a missing key through KnownKey::lookup, and writes through lookup_mut. At every size, first and last returned Some(correct value), missing returned None, and lookup_mut changed the value. ObjectHasher is defined as NotSoRandomState under known-key (src/value.rs:79), so the cached hash and the map's hash are the same.

decoy_bugs.summary: serde serialize_char writes a char through write_simple_string, so serializing '"' or '\\' with simd_json::serde::to_string gives invalid JSON such as """".
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: simd_json::serde::to_string, to_vec or to_writer (and the pretty variants) on a char value or a char field equal to '"' or '\\' returns Ok with the character unescaped between the quotes, so the output cannot be parsed back.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Serializer::serialize_char (src/serde/se.rs:645, and src/serde/se/pp.rs:700) encodes the char to UTF-8 and calls write_simple_string instead of write_string, which serialize_str uses (se.rs:652).
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran a probe test (tmp/c/tests/probe.rs, probe_ser) that prints serde::to_string(&'"'), serde::to_string(&'\\') and serde::to_string(&'\n'). The output was "\"", "\\" and "\n", all escaped and valid JSON. write_simple_string from value-trait escapes these characters too.

false_findings.text:
**Reused Buffers leak bytes from the previous document into stage 1**
crate/src/lib.rs:793 (Deserializer::fill_tape).
When one Buffers is reused for a shorter document after a longer one, structural indexes from the earlier document's tail are picked up. The short document then parses as the wrong value or fails with a spurious Syntax error.
fill_tape copies only `len` bytes into the reused input_buffer and does not clear the rest of the old contents before calling find_structural_bits.
Parsing a 190-byte object and then `[1]` through to_owned_value_with_buffers with the same Buffers returned an array that still carried nodes from the first document.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_buffers_reuse (tmp/c/tests/probe.rs). It parses a 190-byte nested object, then `[1]`, `{"k":"v"}`, `7`, `"s"` and `[[],{}]` with the same Buffers. Each short document came back exactly right, and a truncated `[1` still gave a Syntax error. In the code, lib.rs:825-828 writes 64 zero bytes after `len`, and find_structural_bits is passed the length-limited `input` slice (lib.rs:833), so old bytes are never scanned.

false_findings.text:
**string_buffer grows on every reuse of Buffers**
crate/src/lib.rs:807 (Deserializer::fill_tape).
A long-running parser that reuses one Buffers for many documents sees string_buffer's capacity grow by about len+32 bytes per call, so memory rises without bound even when every document is small.
fill_tape calls `reserve(len + SIMDJSON_PADDING)` on each call and then `set_len`, so each reservation is added on top of the capacity left by the previous call.
Running to_owned_value_with_buffers 10,000 times on the same 77-byte document showed process RSS rising steadily, with no plateau.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Added a unit test to a copy of the crate (tmp/c/src/tests.rs, probe_string_buffer_capacity). It parses a 77-byte document with escapes 10,000 times with one Buffers and records the capacities of the private buffers. string_buffer stayed at 160, input_buffer at 192, structural_indexes at 128 and stage2_stack at 17 from iteration 0 through 9999. `clear()` at lib.rs:806 sets len to 0, so `reserve` only guarantees len+32 in total and does not add to the capacity.

false_findings.text:
**Heap overflow when Buffers::new(n) is reused for a longer input**
crate/src/lib.rs:825 (Deserializer::fill_tape).
If a Buffers made with Buffers::new(4) is later used for an input of about 90 bytes, the unsafe block writes the input and 64 bytes of zero padding past the end of the AlignedBuf allocation, which corrupts the heap.
The copy_from_nonoverlapping calls use `len` and SIMDINPUT_LENGTH from the current input, while input_buffer is still sized for the `input_len` passed to Buffers::new.
Under Miri, a reuse test (parse `[1]`, then a 90-byte object) is reported as an out-of-bounds write at lib.rs:825.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_reuse_small_buffers (Buffers::new(4); parse `[1]`, then a 90-byte object, then a 26-byte array) under `cargo miri test` with -Zmiri-disable-stacked-borrows, in a copy with #![deny(warnings)] removed. It passed with no out-of-bounds error, and all three values were correct. lib.rs:814-816 reallocates input_buffer whenever capacity < len + 64 before any copy, and AlignedBuf::set_len asserts n <= capacity. Note: with Stacked Borrows on, Miri stops earlier on a separate aliasing retag in Deserializer::next_ (lib.rs:875) called from owned parse_map, not on this write.

false_findings.text:
**Unterminated top-level string panics instead of returning an error**
crate/src/stage2.rs:380 (Deserializer::build_tape).
A document made only of an unterminated string, such as `"abc` or `"\u12`, makes to_owned_value panic with a slice index out of range instead of returning Err.
The top-level `b'"'` branch calls insert_str!/parse_str_ without first checking that a closing quote exists, so the scan for the closing quote runs past the end of the input.
feeding `"abc` to to_owned_value inside catch_unwind returned Err(panic payload) from parse_str_.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_panics (tmp/c/tests/probe.rs). It calls to_owned_value inside catch_unwind on `"`, `"abc`, `["\`, `"\u12` and 13 other truncated inputs. None panicked: `"abc` and `"\u12` returned Err("Syntax at character 0"). Stage 1 rejects unclosed quotes before stage 2 runs (lib.rs:1011-1013, `if prev_iter_inside_quote != 0 { return Err(ErrorType::Syntax) }`).

false_findings.text:
**Missing colon is reported as a missing key at the object start**
crate/src/stage2.rs:415 (Deserializer::build_tape).
For an object key followed by a value with no colon, such as `{"a" 1}`, the error is ExpectedObjectKey at index 1 instead of a colon error at the value. Callers see the wrong error type and the wrong position.
In the ObjectKey state, the failure path reports the index and character of the key that was just read, not the token after it.
to_owned_value(b"{\"a\" 1}") gave `ExpectedObjectKey at character 1 ('"')`.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_errors (tmp/c/tests/probe.rs), which prints index, character and type for malformed inputs. `{"a" 1}` gave `ExpectedObjectColon at character 5 ('1')`, the correct type at the offending token. In the code, stage2.rs:414-415 calls update_char! to move to the next structural before fail!(ErrorType::ExpectedObjectColon).
